skill.name: tester-brand-probe
skill.description: diconium brand rules for slides and documents: colours, Campton type, the CAPS and lowercase rules, tone of voice and imagery. Use when creating or restyling any diconium deck or document.
skill.body:
# diconium brand

Apply this whenever you produce something that carries the diconium name — a deck, a one-pager, a
document, a diagram. It was built to restyle PowerPoint into the corporate identity, and the same
rules apply to anything else visual.

Derived from the official **diconium Design Guide, October 2024** (73 pages) plus the current company
presentation, via a design system built in Claude Design in June 2026. Rules below cite the guide's
own page numbers where they exist, so anything here can be checked against the source.

## The five rules people get wrong

**"diconium" is always lowercase.** In running copy, in headlines, at the start of a sentence, always.
Never "Diconium". This is the single most visible mistake and it is the one people notice.

**CAPS only up to 30 characters.** Primary headlines may be set in CAPS when they are 30 characters
or shorter — `UPDATING INDUSTRIES`, `DESIRABLE FUTURES`. Longer than that, use lowercase. Secondary
headlines and all body copy are lowercase always. If a document mixes long and short headings, drop
CAPS entirely rather than mixing the two.

**White dominates.** Roughly 70% of a layout is white. Orange, black and purple are accents, not
fields. Orange `#FF5000` is the hero accent, black is mainly text, purple is reserved for short
highlights, quotes and calls to action. Balance is judged across a body of work, not on one slide.

**Square corners, flat surfaces.** The identity is geometric and sharp. Default corner radius is 0.
Prefer line and colour steps over shadows and glows. Avoid gradients as decoration — the one
exception is the signature warm-orange to cool-teal resonance wash.

**No emoji.** Not part of the brand voice, anywhere.

## Colours

Primary is orange `#FF5000`, white `#FFFFFF`, black `#000000`. Secondary is purple `#581F9D`. There
is a phase-2 blue `#003E96` that is **not** used yet — do not reach for it.

Each brand colour has a resonance ramp at 80/60/40/20%. Full values, greyscale and the semantic
aliases are in `references/colors.md`.

## Type

**Campton** (René Bieder) across the full weight range. Headlines are Extra Bold and tight, body is
Book. Official fallback is **Tenorite**, then a system sans.

Campton is a **commercially licensed typeface and its font files are deliberately not shipped with
this skill** — see the note at the bottom. On a diconium machine Campton is installed already, so
naming the font is enough for PowerPoint and Word to render it correctly. Casing rules, the weight
map and the type scale are in `references/typography-and-casing.md`.

## Voice

Confident, forward-looking, plain-spoken. Optimistic but precise. "we" for diconium, "you" for the
client. Numbers are used as proof points and set large — 2,500 experts, 30 years, 100% Volkswagen
Group subsidiary, since 1995. Avoid hype words; favour concrete value.

Tagline is **"Updating industries"** — it is a message, not a signature, and never sits under the
logo. The signature lines that should be quoted verbatim are in `references/voice-and-copy.md`.

## Resonance

The heart of the identity, and the part most often missed. Resonance means echo — empathy causing
things to vibrate in sympathy. It appears three ways: the symbol (the diconium D echoed into decaying
arcs), the resonance grid (vertical columns at ¼X · X · X · X · 2X), and the resonance image filter
(vertical striping with a warm-orange to cool-teal wash, used for data, digital and AI subjects).

Never apply the resonance filter to cars or to client imagery. Imagery rules, including the 80/20
black-and-white ratio for people photography, are in `references/imagery-and-layout.md`.

## Working on PowerPoint

This is what the design system was built for. `references/powerpoint.md` has the RGB values in the
form python-pptx wants, the font names to set, slide geometry, and the checks worth running before
handing a deck back.

One caveat carried over from the source: the official diconium template `.potx` failed to upload when
the design system was built, so the slide layouts were reconstructed from the company presentation
PDF rather than matched to the real masters. If you have the `.potx`, use it as the starting file and
apply these rules on top rather than rebuilding a deck from scratch.

## Reference files

- `references/colors.md` — every colour token, the resonance ramps, greyscale, semantic roles.
- `references/typography-and-casing.md` — the weight map, type scale, line height, tracking, and the
  casing rules in full.
- `references/voice-and-copy.md` — tone, person, the verbatim signature lines, the proof-point numbers.
- `references/imagery-and-layout.md` — imagery categories, the resonance system, spacing, the grid.
- `references/powerpoint.md` — applying all of it to a .pptx, with the values in usable form.
- `assets/brand/` — logo lockups and symbols in orange, black and white.

## About the fonts

The 18 Campton `.otf` files that came with the original design system are **not** included here, for
two reasons. Campton is a paid typeface licensed from its foundry, and redistributing the binaries to
everyone in the company through a cloud service is a licensing question that needs answering rather
than assuming. And for the actual job it is unnecessary — PowerPoint and Word use the copy of Campton
installed on the machine, so naming the font produces correct output without shipping it.

If a rendering job genuinely needs the font embedded, and licensing has been checked, the files can be
added under a `fonts/` folder in this skill. Until then, name the font and let the local install do the
work. Where neither Campton nor Tenorite is available, the fallback is a system sans — flag that the
output is off-brand rather than silently substituting something else.

references.text:
# Type and casing

Source: diconium Design Guide 2024, "Typography", p.37–43.

## The family

**Campton**, by René Bieder, is the primary face, used across its full range in roman and italic.
Official fallback is **Tenorite**, then a system sans.

| Weight | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Thin | 100 | Very-thin standalone key messages only |
| ExtraLight | 200 | |
| Light | 300 | |
| **Book** | **400** | **Body copy** |
| Medium | 500 | |
| SemiBold | 600 | |
| Bold | 700 | |
| **ExtraBold** | **800** | **Headlines** |
| Black | 900 | Very-heavy standalone key messages only |

Thin and Black are reserved for key messages standing on their own. Do not use them for headings in
a normal deck.

## Casing — the identity device

This is where the brand is won or lost, and it is the part an assistant will get wrong by default.

**"diconium" is always all-lowercase.** In body copy, in headlines, at the start of a sentence,
in a bulleted list. Never "Diconium", never "DICONIUM" unless the whole headline is legitimately in
CAPS and under the character limit.

**Primary headlines** may be CAPS **when they are 30 characters or fewer**. Above 30 characters they
are lowercase. Count the characters — this is a hard rule from the guide, not a feel.

**Secondary headlines are always lowercase.** **Body copy is always lowercase.**

**If a document mixes long and short headlines, drop CAPS altogether** and set everything lowercase.
Consistency beats the device.

CAPS are an active identity choice for short, punchy key messages. They are not a way to add emphasis
to an ordinary heading.

## Scale

Based on a 16px root.

| Role | Size |
|---|---|
| Display, hero key messages | 72px |
| H1 | 48px |
| H2 | 36px |
| H3 | 24px |
| H4 | 20px |
| Lead paragraph | 22px |
| Body | 16px |
| Small | 14px |
| Caption | 12px |
| Overline, CAPS labels | 11px |

## Line height and tracking

Line height: 1.05 for large CAPS display, 1.15 for headlines, 1.5 for body, 1.65 relaxed.

Tracking: −0.02em tight, 0 normal, **0.04em on CAPS headlines**, 0.12em on overlines. CAPS need the
extra tracking — set without it they read as cramped.

# Applying the brand to PowerPoint

This is what the design system was originally built for: taking an arbitrary deck and restyling it
into the diconium identity.

## Start from the template if you have it

The official diconium template (`27052025_Companyslides_2025_V005_.potx` at the time of writing) is
the correct starting point, because it carries the real slide masters and layouts. When the design
system was built, that file failed to upload, so its slide layouts are **reconstructed from the
company presentation PDF rather than matched to the masters**.

So: if the `.potx` is available, open it and apply these rules on top. Only rebuild from scratch when
it genuinely is not available, and say so in the handover.

## Colours as RGB

python-pptx wants `RGBColor(r, g, b)`.

| Name | Hex | RGB |
|---|---|---|
| orange | `#FF5000` | 255, 80, 0 |
| black | `#000000` | 0, 0, 0 |
| white | `#FFFFFF` | 255, 255, 255 |
| purple | `#581F9D` | 88, 31, 157 |
| orange 80 | `#FF7333` | 255, 115, 51 |
| orange 60 | `#FF9666` | 255, 150, 102 |
| orange 40 | `#FFB999` | 255, 185, 153 |
| orange 20 | `#FFDCCC` | 255, 220, 204 |
| purple 80 | `#794CB1` | 121, 76, 177 |
| purple 60 | `#9B79C4` | 155, 121, 196 |
| grey 80 | `#333333` | 51, 51, 51 |
| grey 60 | `#666666` | 102, 102, 102 |
| grey 20 | `#CCCCCC` | 204, 204, 204 |
| grey 05 | `#F2F2F2` | 242, 242, 242 |

Do not use the phase-2 blue `#003E96` — it is not in the launch palette.

## Fonts

Set the font **by name**: `Campton`, with `Tenorite` as the documented fallback.

The font files are not shipped with this skill on purpose — Campton is licensed, and a diconium
machine already has it installed, so naming it is enough for PowerPoint to render correctly. If the
deck will be opened somewhere Campton is not installed, say so rather than silently substituting.

Headlines are **Campton ExtraBold** (weight 800). Body is **Campton Book** (weight 400). Thin and
Black weights are for standalone key messages only.

## Slide geometry

16:9. Build on an 8px grid. White is the default background and should stay dominant — resist the
urge to fill slides with orange.

Square corners on every shape. Flat fills. No drop shadows, no glows, no decorative gradients.

## The casing pass — do this one explicitly

Restyling a deck is not only colours and fonts. Run a pass over every text frame:

1. Every occurrence of "Diconium" or "DICONIUM" in running copy becomes **"diconium"**.
2. Primary headlines of 30 characters or fewer may be CAPS. Longer ones become lowercase.
3. Secondary headlines and body copy become lowercase.
4. If the deck mixes long and short headlines, drop CAPS entirely and set all of them lowercase.
5. Remove any emoji.

This is the pass that makes a deck actually look like diconium, and it is the one most likely to be
skipped because it changes the words rather than the styling.

## Logos

`assets/brand/` holds the lockup and the symbol in orange, black and white. Pick the variant by
background: orange or black lockup on white, white lockup on a dark or photographic background.

The tagline "Updating industries" **never sits under the logo**. It is a message used on covers, not
part of the lock-up.

## Before handing it back

Check: is white still carrying most of the layout, or has it turned into an orange deck? Is
"diconium" lowercase everywhere? Are any headlines in CAPS above 30 characters? Are corners square?
Are there stray gradients or shadows? Did any emoji survive? Is the resonance filter on a car or a
client image, where it must not be?

# Colours

Source: diconium Design Guide 2024, "Colors", p.44–47.

## Brand core

| Token | Hex | RGB | Pantone | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| orange | `#FF5000` | 255, 80, 0 | Orange 021 C | Hero accent |
| white | `#FFFFFF` | 255, 255, 255 | — | Dominant base, ~70% of a layout |
| black | `#000000` | 0, 0, 0 | — | Mainly text |
| purple | `#581F9D` | 88, 31, 157 | 267 C | Secondary, short highlights and quotes |
| blue | `#003E96` | 0, 62, 150 | 2146 C | **Phase 2 — not in use, do not apply** |

## Resonance steps

Solid tints on white, not opacity. The colour-step system is part of the identity.

**Orange** — `#FF5000` (100) · `#FF7333` (80) · `#FF9666` (60) · `#FFB999` (40) · `#FFDCCC` (20) · `#FFF1EA` (08, faint wash for fills and hover surfaces)

**Purple** — `#581F9D` (100) · `#794CB1` (80) · `#9B79C4` (60) · `#BCA5D8` (40) · `#DED2EB` (20)

**Blue, phase 2, unused** — `#003E96` (100) · `#3365AB` (80) · `#668BC0` (60) · `#99B2D5` (40) · `#CCD8EA` (20)

## Greyscale

`#000000` · `#1A1A1A` (90) · `#333333` (80) · `#666666` (60) · `#999999` (40) · `#CCCCCC` (20) · `#E6E6E6` (10) · `#F2F2F2` (05) · `#FFFFFF`

## Semantic roles

Accent is orange. Accent hover darkens to `#E64800`, pressed to `#CC4000`. Secondary accent is purple.

Background is white; subtle background is `#F2F2F2`; inverse background is black. Body text is black,
muted text is `#666666`, inverse text is white, text on the accent is white.

Borders are `#CCCCCC`, strong borders black. Focus ring is a 2px orange outline.

Functional states stay inside the palette where possible: success `#1F8A5B`, warning is the brand
orange, danger `#C72A1C`, info is the phase-2 blue (so in practice avoid it until blue is live).

## Using them

White carries the layout. Orange is an accent and loses its force the moment it becomes a field —
a full orange slide is off-brand. Purple is for short highlights, quotes and calls to action, not
for body text or large areas. Balance is judged across a set of slides, not one at a time.

# Voice and copy

## Tone

Confident, forward-looking, plain-spoken thought leadership. Optimistic but precise. The brand
positions itself as a thought leader that "updates industries".

Avoid hype words. Favour concrete value — "more efficient, profitable, competitive" rather than
"revolutionary" or "cutting-edge". Where a claim can be made with a number, use the number.

## Person

**"we"** for diconium. **"you" / "your"** for the client. The register is collective and
partnership-oriented — "collective competence", "experts with empathy".

## Signature lines

Use these verbatim when they fit. Do not paraphrase them.

**Tagline** — "Updating industries". It is a message, not a lock-up element: it appears on covers
and on the website, and it **never sits under the logo**.

**One-liner** — "diconium is a global group building software delivery organizations."

**Value proposition** — "We navigate complexity and deliver competitiveness at scale."

**Rhetorical hook**, recurring — "future businesses don't need to be more digital. they need to be
smarter."

## The why / how / what framework

**Why** — updating industries and societies to build desirable futures.
**How** — empathy, diverse teams of experts, value creation.
**What** — we build software delivery organizations.

## Proof points

Used as bold numbers, set large. 2,500 experts. 30 years. 100% Volkswagen Group subsidiary. Present
in 4 of the 5 leading economies. Founded 1995. Around 2,500 experts across hubs in 6 countries.

diconium is a global digital business-transformation group, a wholly owned subsidiary of the
Volkswagen Group, generating value from software, data and AI, with a strong e-commerce heritage.

Named client success stories that appear in the company presentation: STIHL, MANN+HUMMEL, Bechtle,
Endress+Hauser, Kodak Alaris, TRUMPF.

## Hard rules

**No emoji.** Not part of the brand voice, in any medium.

**"diconium" is always lowercase**, including at the start of a sentence. See the casing reference.

Do not invent statistics or client names. If a number is needed and not listed here, ask for it
rather than producing a plausible one — these appear in client-facing material.

# Imagery, resonance and layout

## The resonance system

The heart of the identity, and the thing that makes a layout read as diconium rather than as a
generic orange deck. "Resonance" means echo or reverberation — empathy causing things to vibrate in
sympathy. It shows up three ways.

**The symbol** — the diconium "D" echoed into decaying arcs, a reverberating mark. It can be cropped
by the format and used as a framing device, not only as a logo.

**The resonance grid** — vertical columns at proportional widths **¼X · X · X · X · 2X**. Use it to
structure editorial layouts and to crop imagery.

**The resonance image filter** — vertical line and glitch striping over photography, usually with a
warm-orange to cool-teal colour wash. Reserved for data, digital and AI subjects.

**Never apply the resonance filter to cars, or to client imagery.**

## Imagery categories

**Diverse experts** — real employee portraits, roughly **80% black and white, 20% colour**. The ratio
inverts to mostly colour for employer branding. A subtle light texture may be added but **never
between the subject and the viewer**. No stock photography.

**The big picture** — large-scale, impact, global reach. Colour or black and white.

**Clients** — the client's own product or headquarters imagery, used **unedited and never filtered**.

**Data and abstract** — abstract or detail shots through the resonance filter, in black and white,
natural colour, or orange combined with purple or blue.

Overall colour vibe: warm orange highlights against cool teal and blue shadows, high contrast.

## Form and surface

Geometric and sharp. **Default corner radius is 0** — a 2 to 4px softening exists but is secondary.
Surfaces are flat. Depth is restrained: prefer line and colour steps over shadows and glows.

**Avoid gradients as decoration.** The one sanctioned gradient is the warm-to-cool resonance wash.

Border widths: 1px thin, 2px medium, 3px thick. Focus ring is a 2px orange outline.

## Layout and spacing

White space is active and intentional — the guide's words are "calmness and professionalism". White
carries roughly 70% of a layout.

Build on an **8px grid**. The spacing scale is 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128px. Maximum
content container is 1200px.

Use the resonance column ratios for editorial layouts and image crops rather than an even grid.

## Motion

Calm and professional. Short fades and clean transitions, 120–400ms, standard easing. **No bounces**
and no playful overshoot.

Hover darkens orange to `#E64800`, or fills an outline to solid. Press darkens further to `#CC4000`.
No scale-shrink on press for buttons. Cards lift about 2px on hover.

## Icons

diconium ships **no proprietary icon set**. The identity carries through the symbol, the resonance
grid, CAPS typography and photography rather than spot icons.

The one recurring glyph is the arrow **→** on "read more" and "learn more" actions, set in the brand
font rather than an icon font.

If a piece genuinely needs functional icons, use a thin geometric outline set that matches Campton's
character — around 1.75px stroke, square joins, monochrome in black or orange for an active state.
Avoid filled and duotone styles. Treat this as a documented substitution and say so, because it is
not part of the official brand.

No emoji and no decorative unicode glyphs as iconography.
